chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about cupping and shaving the back of the neck during the months of Hajj, so he said, 'There is no harm with it and with the nurah.'

The meaning of his saying 'shaving the back of the neck during the months of Hajj' is those that are other than Dhu al-Qi'dah, such as Shawwal, because it is permissible for a man to shave his head and the back of his neck in this month. What was narrated indicates that:

key_terms.حَلْقُ اَلْقَفَا: Shaving the back of the neck

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to shave one's head or back of the neck during the Hajj months in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the restrictions on grooming during the sacred months of Hajj do not extend to Shawwal, thereby permitting cupping, shaving the head and nape, and using depilatories. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the specific prohibitions of the Hajj months and general permissibility, emphasizing ease in personal hygiene for pilgrims. The inclusion of 'nurah' underscores the comprehensive nature of these allowances, covering both hair removal and skin care.
